text:
Mackenzie Blackwood stopped all 27 shots Detroit threw at him, and Colorado turned a lopsided middle period into a 4-0 win at Ball Arena. Blackwood was drafted 42nd overall in 2015 and spent time in the ECHL with Adirondack in 2017-18 before reaching the NHL. On this night, he got his shutout and a second-star nod.

The result was never in doubt after the second period, but the first and third were closer than the score suggests. Detroit had the better of the first period in expected goals (a measure of shot quality), 0.95 to 0.72. Then Colorado took over, out-chancing the Red Wings 2.00 to 0.30 in the second, and Martin Necas opened the scoring on the power play at 9:46. Nathan MacKinnon made it 2-0 on another power play less than three minutes later. Overall, our numbers say Colorado deserved to win 73 percent of the time, meaning it takes that share of simulated replays of every shot.

Detroit finished 0 for 3 on the power play while Colorado went 3 for 5. Necas, taken 12th overall in 2017 out of HC Kometa Brno, added an even-strength goal in the third and finished with two goals and two assists. Cale Makar sealed it with a wrist shot on a 4 percent chance. Blackwood saved about two goals more than the quality of the shots he faced would predict, while Daniil Tarasov allowed four on 29 shots for Detroit. The data here doesn't carry either team's record or streak, so we'll leave it at the shutout.
